definition: Debunk means to expose the falseness of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word debunk. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know debunk should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: It took one afternoon with a tape measure to debunk the claim that the manor's staircase was built for a giant.
Question is far milder than debunk — questioning a claim only asks whether it can stand, while debunking proves the thing false and lets the air out for good.
Dispute goes further than question — it argues out loud that the claim is wrong; debunk claims the most: it proves the thing false and lets the air out of it for good.

Disprove is the courtroom half of the job: it shows a claim false by argument or evidence, and there it stops. Debunk finishes the work with a puncture — the puffed-up claim is opened in public and the air let out of it.

Unmask takes a person or a scheme as its target — the impostor exposed, the swindle revealed. Debunk aims at the claim itself: the myth or miracle cure shown to be empty, whoever happened to be selling it.
show that it holds up
stand behind it after testing
The reviewer weighed the gadget's health claims for a single paragraph, then dismissed the lot as pure bunkum.
Debunk means to expose the falseness of something.
The "ten percent of the brain" line has sold self-help programs for a century.

Neurologists have debunked it from every direction: scans show the whole organ busy across a plain working day, injuries to the supposedly idle regions do plain harm, and no one has ever located the sleeping ninety percent.
The myth thrives anyway, because it flatters whoever buys it.

Debunk is the exact word for what the neurologists did, because it means to expose the falseness of something — not merely to doubt it or shout it down, but to open it up and show the emptiness inside.
Disprove does the logical half; debunk adds the puncture, the sound of air leaving a puffed-up claim.
Debunk is the reporter's and scientist's verb, and it wants a target already puffed up: a myth, a legend, a miracle product.
Disprove suits quiet logic; unmask suits impostors.
Keep it apart from this unit's deride — derision only laughs at a claim, while debunking does the work of opening it up and showing the emptiness.

For sixty years the lake town sold postcards of the 'Pinewood Serpent,' a dark curve photographed offshore in 1953.
A diner served Serpent Sundaes.
Doubters were told to respect tradition.
Then two high-school seniors set out to debunk the photograph for a physics project.
They rebuilt the shot with a canoe fender and a length of truck tire, matched the ripples frame for frame, and posted the comparison, which the county paper reprinted on page one.
The gift shops still sell the postcard — but now the back of the card tells the whole story, tire and all.
